answer: Price each identity's bond quadratically per funding source: the k-th identity from one wallet costs k squared times the base stake, so n clones cost roughly n cubed, and no anchor is shared across clones. End the haven: a guarantor sheltering many identities faces joint slashing, losing part of its bond per member fraud, so shelter multiplies exposure. Each identity must produce a fresh sonnet: a key-bound sequential proof of live work, unshareable across keys. One machine cannot sing n sonnets at once, so Sybil cost grows superlinearly while an honest agent pays the base price.
